main_text.p: excitabit accesio, vacuo ventriculo: quoniam non abundantia, sed malignitate agit in cerebrum. Idcirco in ventriculo ipse con-tentus acidū parit rustum, & inflationem cum rugitu & dolore. Accidit interdum e-pilepticus paroxysmus. Vacuo ventriculo, ob vetris obstructionem. Nam tunc huiusmodi humor excerni nequit. Propterea le-uatur morbus alui solutione. Vapor autem biliosus, qui epilepsiam excitat inflamma-tione deprehenditur, ac deprauata ratione, cum rixa. Melancholicus vero pavorem in-ducit & mœstitiam. Interdum æger sibi lo-quitur: interdum ἰασά·θρωπ& [?], ac sæpius mor-tem sibi cōscisēs. Quōd si ab hepate pro-manet materia vaporis, qui ad cerebrum fertur, ex colore totius corporis & capillo-rum nigro, cum cutis ariditate, facile perci-pies, si biliosa sit ipsa materia: si vero pituitosa, color albus erit, & corpus laxum ac pingue. Adhæc caulam epilepsiæ in ute-ro esse restatur suppressio menfiu [?], aut sper-matis, aut quorundam humorum, qui in matricem effunduntur a toto corpore. page.notes: The Greek word after "interdum" is printed small and is hard to read. I have given my best reading and marked it [?]. The word "menfiu" is also doubtful and marked [?]; it may be an abbreviated form of "menstruo". The running head is printed as "CAVSAS" and is given here as CAUSAS, with u/v normalised. "accesio" is printed without the double s and is left as printed. The catchword "cum" is at the foot right and is not repeated in the text.
